title: ScaleAuto Pro Track

scope.basis: Track, borders and mounting accessories depicted on the current official Pro Track catalogue panels, reviewed October 2026.
excluded: Complete starter-set layouts and their non-track electronics
Unidentified R1 22.5-degree pieces shown in the dimension diagram without mapped catalogue SKUs
Custom sponsor graphics; generic graphic placeholders are supplied
scope.availability: Includes catalogue-announced special pieces. Listing is not proof of retail availability, installed digital hardware or compatibility with a particular digital protocol.

defaults.note: Road width, lane spacing and radius boundaries are published. Centred slot offsets are derived. 48 mm is explicitly shown for straight borders; its application to curve borders is an assumption.

visualStyle.road: Medium grey with a slight green cast and subtle surface texture, plain without centre dashes
visualStyle.borders: Plain matching grey based on product photographs; custom-print border is a separate variant
visualStyle.rails: Paired silver rails with dark slots; moulded tabs and silver contact tips
visualStyle.accessories: Separate red/white guardrail types, orange/white fixing links, metal clips and white flexible wall
visualStyle.basis: Official catalogue photographs and diagrams. Original SVG drawings, not reproduced product images.

sourceIssues.detail: Panel 07 labels its 200 mm road SC-10105, also used there for an R2 inner border. Panel 04 and the starter-set inventory identify the road as SC-10005; the latter is used.
Panel 06 shortens/mistypes the base codes as SC-1001c / SC-1000d. Normalized to the SC-10001 straight family, with letter suffixes; confirm commercial SKU before ordering.

Overview geometry has red/white kerbs, but standard product photographs show plain grey mouldings. Artwork follows product photographs; pit schematic and custom-print variants are separately labelled.
Diagram items 25–27 have no unambiguous product-code mapping in the inspected panels and are excluded rather than assigned invented SKUs.
